Blah - went to edit my post but hit delete.

Anyway I was saying something along the lines that it doesn't particularly matter if I see it as a target or not. In the context of the trade, it was a rally base drop, that price pushed into, I took a market order, I set a stoploss above the high, and I set a take profit below price. There was a little analysis on the HTF to make sure it was in confluence. There wasn't much more thought process than that. The edge is in the risk:reward ratio I achieve from taking many of these types of trades.

I highly recommend just posting into your journal if you want to progress your understanding of the markets. The process of scribbling on your own charts, justifying your own decision making will allow you to come to terms with the gaps in your knowledge.

Hope this helps.

Guys you're over thinking it. I take lots of trades. I lose lots of trades. Yeah that's right, I lose and I love it, it frees my mind up to reanalyse and focus on new opportunities! I suffered a long time trying to be a perfectionist but ultimately you cannot be right 100% of the time so create your edge elsewhere! Something like 50-60% of the time I get stopped out for 5-15 pips. I share the ones that look pretty and I purposely leave my stop where it is (instead of moving it to BE out of FEAR) so you can see the ridiculous risk:reward I achieve. The edge is pretty much in everything else in your trading plan that isn't your entry.

Here take this for example. This is just having a bit of fun but look past that and see that I simply took retests at new demand with minor s/r as confluence in an uptrend. The ones that failed did not sit at the right spots and I was punished, but I was able to refocus on the task at hand as a positive outcome of failing.

Not every trade you take has to be some picture perfect S/R that you looked at in a text book. Immerse yourself in the market and follow what price is intending to do.

The aftermath

Ok now you're just showing off;-)

Yes, perfectionism - I've suffered from this my whole life in every area, not just trading. I feel insulted when I take a loss. But it's holding me back now, I realise. I can win 20 trades in a row, and frequently do, doubling or trebling my account in a week - and then I give the whole lot back because I'm badly wrong, once. It's got to stop.

Thanks for the candour about how may you lose - this definitely makes me rethink what I'm doing.

Away
